messages.author: d1237c2d244e29ff
messages.subject: A Wierd Softmax Regression Parameterization Issue
parts:
In a standard Softmax model, I could write:
 for(p in 1:P){
 for(m in 1:(M-1)){
#################################################################################### Link
   Alpha[m,p] <- Theta[m,1] +  Theta[m,2]*Predictor1[p] + Theta[m,3]*Predictor2[p];
             }
   Alpha[M,p] <- 0; # Fix one outcome at 0

#################################################################################### Model Data
  Outcome[p]~ multinomial(softmax(Alpha[p]));
}

However, I have predictors unique to a category of outcome:
 for(p in 1:P){
 for(m in 1:(M-1)){
#################################################################################### Link
   Alpha[m,p] <- Theta[m,1] +  Theta[m,2]*Predictor1[m,p] + Theta[m,3]*Predictor2[m,p];
             }
   Alpha[M,p] <- 0; # Fix one outcome at 0

#################################################################################### Model Data
  Outcome[p]~ multinomial(softmax(Alpha[p]));
}

So the code above doesn't seem to make sense, as is.

 However, it would make sense to rewrite the model as:
 for(p in 1:P){
 for(m in 1:(M-1)){
#################################################################################### Link
   Alpha[m,p] <- Theta[m,1] +  Theta[m,2]*Predictor1m1[p] + Theta[m,3]*Predictor2m1[p] +   Theta[m,4]*Predictor1m2[p] + Theta[m,5]*Predictor2m2[p] +  Theta[m,6]*Predictor1m3[p] +    Theta[m,7]*Predictor2m3[p]  + etc...
 
          }
   Alpha[M,p] <- 0; # Fix one outcome at 0

#################################################################################### Model Data
  Outcome[p]~ multinomial(softmax(Alpha[p]));
}
where each Predictor for each category m1, m2, m3, etc... is specifically encoded in the model.

But this has too many parameters... So I'd like to fix most of them to zero, specifically Theta[1,4]-Theta[1,7], Theta[2,2]-Theta[2,3], Theta[2,6]-Theta[2,7], Theta[2,4]-Theta[3,5] above.

By fixing these parameter values to zero, I keep the standard model notation for the softmax regression, but I also keep the spirit of the first model I tried to write.

However, the line:
 Alpha[M,p] <- 0; # Fix one outcome at 0

no longer seem to make sense to me, since I am not actually using one predictor to predict M outcomes using M (or even M-1) parameters.

Any suggestions as to how I should define this model? I know I haven't phrase the question is a very good way, but I'm a little blocked on how to describe this issue.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] A Wierd Softmax Regression Parameterization Issue
parts:
You can do softmax with K parameters instead of K-1.
It's just that you need priors to identify the result if
everything's free. Given that you have a regression you're
using, then you might just need to get rid of extra intercepts.

- Bob

messages.author: d1237c2d244e29ff
messages.subject: Re: A Wierd Softmax Regression Parameterization Issue
parts:
Bob,

I still don't quite understand your response. You use the plural "extra intercepts" and "them" but isn't there only a single extra intercept?

What I have a regression model for each category of outcome. Each outcome has its own predictor variables that don't factor in to other categories. This is just like writing the model in standard notation (and including every predictor variable for every category of outcome) with the constraint that parameters are zero for all predictors other than those that correspond to the outcome of interest. As such, I think all of the predictors should be well identified.

 The only remaining issue should be that I have K intercepts. Setting one of these to a constant, should be enough to identify the model right?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: A Wierd Softmax Regression Parameterization Issue
parts:
> On Jul 29, 2015, at 2:58 PM, Cody Ross <ctr...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
>
> Bob,
>
> I still don't quite understand your response. You use the plural "extra intercepts" and "them" but isn't there only a single extra intercept?
Sorry for the confusion. I was speaking in generalities.

> What I have a regression model for each category of outcome. Each outcome has its own predictor variables that don't factor in to other categories. This is just like writing the model in standard notation (and including every predictor variable for every category of outcome) with the constraint that parameters are zero for all predictors other than those that correspond to the outcome of interest. As such, I think all of the predictors should be well identified.

It's the coefficients that get identified, and the usual problem
is multiple intercepts --- it's a natural feature (or problem) for
hierarchical models. And it's even worse in something like IRT where
there's just obvious problems.
See the manual chapter on problematic posteriors. The standard
hierarchical models are only only weakly identified.

mu_beta ~ ...
beta ~ normal(mu_beta, mu_sigma);
...
y_hat <- x[n] * beta

Because it's identical to having

mu_beta ~ ...
beta_raw ~ normal(0, mu_sigma);

...
> The only remaining issue should be that I have K intercepts. Setting one of these to a constant, should be enough to identify the model right?

I'd think so. But I don't have time to trace through the whole
model to check. If it's not identified, you'll know in the posterior
through high correlations of variables.

- Bob
